authors: Gabriele G.; Pavirani F.; Karimi Madahi S.S.; Develder C.
problem: Single-charger sequential EV charging with unknown departure time (30-min steps, time-varying price)
method: Decision-focused RL (DF-RL): departure-time forecaster trained end-to-end with feedback from the RL charging agent; forecast appended to the state (Sec. 3)
architecture: Actor-critic agent with a learned forecaster; not size-agnostic (one charging point)
environment_or_data: Real sessions from a hospital parking facility (RENergetic project); 20 most frequent users modelled statistically; 350 training / 120 test sessions; fixed 6.5 kW charging power (Sec. 4)
baselines: BAU charge-on-arrival; RL without forecast; RL with MSE-trained forecaster; RL with true departure
key_results: Abstract: up to 14% higher total reward and 55% less unsupplied energy than RL without departure forecasting; conclusion: about 5% reward gain and 14% less unmet energy vs a conventional (MSE) forecaster
limitations: Soft penalty for unmet energy (fixed + quadratic); no coverage or feasibility guarantee; single charger, one price profile; preprint

problem: Charging under a distribution-transformer capacity when deadlines cannot all be met (severe congestion)
method: Offline convex benchmark with transformer aging proxy and penalty-weighted unmet energy at departure; online marginal-cost-aware urgency-index heuristic allocating power sequentially (Sec. II-IV)
architecture: No learning; MDP formulation used only to define the online setting
constraint_handling: penalty+other:soft deadlines, hard transformer/charger limits in feasible action set
environment_or_data: Synthetic case study, e.g. 35 EVs arriving 2-7 PM with 2-5 h slack (Sec. V)
key_results: Online policy approximates the offline benchmark; higher transformer aging but less unmet energy than the offline optimum in the congestion case (Fig. 3, qualitative)
limitations: Not RL; deadlines softened; single author preprint; small case study
evidence_source: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.00935 (curl, grep of Sec. I-V); https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00935

authors: Huang C.; Fan J.; Wang W.; Wang H.
problem: VPP coordinating EV charging stations under partial distribution-network visibility (voltage security + cost)
method: TL-MAPPO: Lagrangian MAPPO (CTDE) with per-station transformer encoder over a temporal observation window (Sec. III-B, III-C)
architecture: Transformer tokens are time steps of one station's observation window, not chargers; one agent per station
environment_or_data: IEEE 33-bus PDN, 4 stations x 10 chargers, 5-min steps; Caltech ACN EV data, Ausgrid PV, AEMO prices (Sec. IV-A)
baselines: MAPPO, MATD3, MASAC; ablation without temporal encoding / with LSTM
key_results: About 45% fewer voltage violations and about 10% lower cost than MARL baselines (abstract)
limitations: Voltage and demand satisfaction only via Lagrangian regularisation; scalability discussed qualitatively (App. B2), not tested; fixed number of stations
evidence_source: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.03278 (preprint of the PESGM paper; curl, grep); abstract via Semantic Scholar

problem: Coordinated fast charging under distribution-feeder constraints (voltage, line/transformer thermal) and queuing
method: Bi-level RL: upper-level GNN coordinator sets station power caps; lower-level station controllers admit EVs and allocate power; action shield runs AC power-flow checks and adjusts caps before execution
architecture: GNN over the IEEE 33-bus feeder graph
key_results: Abstract: shield ensures voltage and thermal limits before execution; grid feasibility and service metrics reported (no numbers in abstract)
limitations: Abstract only; per-step power-flow shield, no departure-energy guarantee stated; fixed feeder
evidence_source: Crossref record 10.1109/iteceats66641.2026.11592825; abstract via Semantic Scholar API

authors: Zhang Z.; Rigo-Mariani R.; Hadjsaid N.; Xu Y.
problem: EV charging management with unknown EV information and transformer thermal loading
method: Comparison of safe DRL categories (constrained-optimisation based, others) for charging management
environment_or_data: Different charger types and ambient temperatures (abstract)
baselines: Uncontrolled charging; several SDRL categories; theoretical optimum
key_results: Constrained-optimisation SDRL delivers >90% of demand, up to 90% fewer violations than uncontrolled charging, 31.7-62.5% closer to the optimum than other SDRL categories (abstract)
limitations: Abstract only; violations reduced, not eliminated; same group as zhang2025modelfree
evidence_source: Crossref record 10.1109/pesgm58988.2026.11693429; abstract via Semantic Scholar API (OA copy listed at hal.science/hal-05704701, not read)
